quotes.citation: མངོན་པར་རྟོགས་པའི་རྒྱན། — chapter 1, the verse listing the ten instructions (གདམས་ངག)
quotes.why: The root verse that names the five eyes as one of the ten instructions; it gives no stages at which they are attained.

quotes.citation: Haribhadra, འགྲེལ་པ་དོན་གསལ། — gloss on the instruction on the five eyes (chapter 1)
quotes.why: Haribhadra defines the five eyes by their objects and calls the divine eye 'born of maturation', but says nothing about the path at which any of them is attained.

quotes.text: ཤའི་སྤྱན་ཚོགས་ལམ་ནས་དང་། ལྷའི་སྤྱན་སྦྱོར་ལམ་དང་། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་སྤྱན་མཐོང་ལམ་དང་། ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྤྱན་མཐོང་ལམ་རྗེས་ཐོབ་ནས་དང་། སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སྤྱན་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ས་དང་། རྗེས་མཐུན་པ་ས་བརྒྱད་པ་ནས་ཡོད་དོ། །
quotes.citation: Gyaltsab Je, རྣམ་བཤད་སྙིང་པོའི་རྒྱན། — chapter 1, on the instruction on the five eyes
quotes.why: The རྣམ་བཤད་ passage the paragraph quotes; note it reads མཐོང་ལམ་ alone for the wisdom eye where the yig cha has མཐོང་ལམ་མཉམ་གཞག་ནས།

quotes.citation: Tsongkhapa, ལེགས་བཤད་གསེར་ཕྲེང་། (stod cha) — chapter 1, the boundaries of the five eyes
quotes.why: The passage the yig cha quotes, in full: the five-stage scheme is reported as what 'earlier scholars' teach, and Tsongkhapa's correction places the concordant Buddha eye at the SEVENTH ground's purification, not the eighth.

quotes.file: Sungbum/PHAR PHYIN_PERFECTION OF WISDOM (PRAJNA PARAMITA) (MADHYAMIKA SVATANTRIKA SCHOOL)/SPYI_GENERAL COMMENTARIES/RJE TZONG KHA PA BLO BZANG GRAGS PA_JE TSONGKAPA LOBSANG DRAKPA (1357-1419)/LEGS BSHAD GSER PHRENG_FINE EXPLANATION, A STRING OF GOLDEN BEADS/S05412TL-1_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I MAN NGAG GI BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN 'GREL PA DANG BCAS PA'I RGYA CHER BSHAD PA'I LEGS BSHAD GSER PHRENG, STOD CHA_Volume I of 'Fine Explanation, a String of Golden Beads,' being an Ex_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Tsongkhapa, ལེགས་བཤད་གསེར་ཕྲེང་། stod cha — the Sungbum edition (S05412TL-1), same place
quotes.why: A second, independent edition of the Golden Garland with the same reading ས་བདུན་པ, so the discrepancy with the yig cha's ས་བརྒྱད་པ is not a slip in one copy.

quotes.citation: Tsongkhapa, ལེགས་བཤད་གསེར་ཕྲེང་། — chapter 1, the boundaries of the six clairvoyances
quotes.why: Tsongkhapa's own ground for putting the divine eye at the accumulation path: the first five clairvoyances are shared with non-Buddhists and present from the great accumulation path.

quotes.file: Tengyur/04 DBU MA_Middle Way School (Madhyamaka)/VOL 14 (AA)/TD03903_THUB PA'I DGONGS PA'I RGYAN (Munimatālaṃkāra)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: The Indian source Tsongkhapa cites as ཐུབ་དགོངས་: the five eyes are attained one by one, with gradations, from the accumulation stage upward — graded acquisition, not fixed thresholds.

quotes.citation: Tsongkhapa, ལེགས་བཤད་གསེར་ཕྲེང་། — chapter 1, quoting a source he calls དག་ལྡན་ on the sixth clairvoyance
quotes.why: A few pages later Tsongkhapa himself cites a source placing the Buddha eye together with the sixth clairvoyance at the eighth ground — the figure the yig cha uses.

quotes.citation: Chökyi Gyaltsen, སྐབས་དང་པོའི་མཐའ་དཔྱོད། — the five eyes, refuting others
quotes.why: The same author in his debate manual names the opponent this paragraph implicitly answers: one who takes the stages as minimum boundaries (མ་མཐའི་ས་མཚམས), refuted with the same two counter-examples.

quotes.citation: Chökyi Gyaltsen, སྐབས་དང་པོའི་མཐའ་དཔྱོད། — the five eyes, own system (རང་ལུགས)
quotes.why: His own gloss of the རྣམ་བཤད་ in the debate manual adds ངེས་པར་, making explicit that the stages mark where an eye is necessarily had, not where it first becomes possible.

quotes.citation: Chökyi Gyaltsen, སྐབས་དང་པོའི་མཐའ་དཔྱོད། — the five eyes, refuting others
quotes.why: Applies the fourth-dhyāna argument of this paragraph to a bodhisattva on the accumulation path, which is how the yig cha squares Tsongkhapa's 'no fault in the accumulation path' with the རྣམ་བཤད།

quotes.citation: Jamyang Zhepa, ཕར་ཕྱིན་མཐའ་དཔྱོད་རིན་ཆེན་སྒྲོན་མེ། — the boundaries of the five eyes
quotes.why: The Gomang textbook sets the Golden Garland (divine eye from the great accumulation path; concordant Buddha eye from the seventh ground) against the རྣམ་བཤད་ (pure grounds) as two readings — it does not merge them as this paragraph does.

quotes.citation: Jamyang Shantipa Lodrö Gyaltsen, སྐབས་བརྒྱད་ཀྱི་སྤྱི་དོན་མེ་ལོང་། — the boundaries of the five eyes
quotes.why: A later overview that adopts this paragraph's hedge in one word, གཙོ་བོར་ཐོབ — 'principally attained' at these stages.
